Commentary.Commentary: Pakistan's bowlers now will have to do a really good job, they need to take early wickets or it is going to be tough for them to get into this game. Let me remind you, they have to bat fourth here on a wicket which seems to be getting tougher. Australia on the other hand, will be eyeing for something over 300. They too will have to bat well for that as the wicket is not easy. An interesting few minutes before the break coming up.

For Pakistan, they started off well but lost Rizwan. Shaheen Afridi and Aamer Jamal also put up a handy partnership. Aamer Jamal played a fighting knock but he will be disappointed with Mir Hamza and Hasan Ali as both failed to stick around with him. The visitors overall will be quite disappointed. They began really well. They were 124 for 1 at one time but once Abdullah Shafique fell, it was a procession. At one time, it seemed like Pakistan would end up giving away a big lead but the likes of Mohammad Rizwan, Aamer Jamal and Shaheen Afridi did well this morning to cut down the deficit to just under 60.

It is Pat Cummins who leads his side off and rightly so! He has probably the reason why his side are in the lead! They will be pleased with how they did this morning, it was not easy as it the outfield was quite wet but Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon were excellent, the two got 9 between them and have ensured their side get a decent lead.

A session that is equally split out between the two teams. Australia started the session in some fashion. Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc with their pin-point accuracy and the skipper followed with the same. Pakistan openers though somehow survived with some closed shaves and a couple of LBW shouts turned down. The pressure was building and something was bound to happen. Nathan Lyon used the pitch quite effectively to get the breakthrough. However, since the arrival of Shan Masood, it has been all Pakistan. They are scoring runs at a good rate and look comfortable. A really interesting final session is coming up which is going to be really long.
